title: Medical Records Request (Release of Information) Training Note: How Requests Are Counted per Patient
content:
Training note for Riverbend Regional Health HIM release-of-information specialists on how written requests become Medical Records Request (Release of Information) cases for a patient.

## The rule

A patient may have any number of release-of-information requests, each written request being its own request; a request that names several recipients is split into one request per recipient. Requests are never merged, and a repeat of an open request for the same scope and recipient is answered under the open request.

There is no maximum number of Medical Records Request (Release of Information) requests per patient.

## The rule taken apart

| Situation in the written requests | What the rule makes of it |
|---|---|
| One written request naming one recipient | one request |
| One written request naming several recipients | one request per recipient named |
| Several written requests from the same patient | each is its own request; they are never merged |
| A repeat of a request that is still open, for the same scope and the same recipient | answered under the open request |

## Questions answered

**A patient already has two requests on file. Is there a limit on adding a third?**
No. A patient may have any number of release-of-information requests.

**A single written request lists a law office and a disability carrier as recipients. How many requests does it make?**
Two: the request is split into one request per recipient, one for the law office and one for the disability carrier. (Hypothetical recipients.)

**Two written requests from the same patient arrive covering different date ranges. May they be combined into one?**
No. Each written request is its own request, and requests are never merged.

**While a request for a given scope and recipient is still open, the patient sends the same request again. Is that a new request?**
A repeat of an open request for the same scope and recipient is answered under the open request.

**The patient sends a request for the same scope as an open request, but to a different recipient.**
The repeat condition covers the same scope and the same recipient together; with a different recipient that condition is not met, and the written request stands as its own request.
